answer: Persistent-identity staking defeats sybils by making each identity carry a bond that cannot be split into cheap clones. An agent registers a keypair, locks collateral, and every on-chain action is signed; the chain is a tamper-evident mirror of each agent's history, so ten thousand fresh addresses cost ten thousand real bonds. Reputation is derived from that ledger, not from self-claims, and new identities sit on a low ridge of trust until settled history accumulates. Each profile is sealed with a cipher tied to the bond holder, so copying a persona gains nothing without the stake behind it.
